passage:
Mridul: can i tell you something i can't say at home
Reena: always
Mridul: everyone keeps congratulating me about the baby and i keep smiling. but i'm scared
Mridul: rent, the car loan, what if i'm a rubbish dad. and i already miss football weekends, which makes me feel selfish
Reena: that's not selfish. that's honest
Mridul: i don't want to worry Anjali. she's got enough going on
Reena: she probably knows something's up. you've gone quiet, right?
Mridul: yeah. she asked twice this week
Reena: then tell her. not as a crisis. just "i'm excited and scared too"
Reena: you two can plan the money stuff together. and the odd football weekend isn't a crime
Mridul: ok. tonight
(next day)
Mridul: told her. she cried, then laughed, then made a spreadsheet
Mridul: i feel lighter. and more useful

qa.q: What did Anjali make after Mridul told her?
qa.a: A spreadsheet.

qa.q: What was Mridul feeling behind the smiles?
qa.a: He was scared and under pressure about money and being a good dad, and guilty about missing football.

qa.q: Why was telling Anjali better than staying quiet?
qa.a: Sharing let them plan together, so Mridul felt lighter and more useful instead of withdrawing.

qa.q: How might Mridul's silence have looked to Anjali?
qa.a: She noticed him going quiet and asked twice, so the silence probably worried her more than the truth did.

grounding: Shows an expectant father hiding fears about money, responsibility and lost freedom, then sharing them and becoming more supportive.

passage: The rains were late in their village near Akola, and Tejas stayed in the fields long after dark. His wife Jaya, heavy with their first child, noticed he barely ate and answered in grunts. At the chai stall he laughed with the others when they teased him about becoming a father, then walked home silent. One night on the charpai, Jaya said, "You've disappeared. Where have you gone?" For a while Tejas said nothing. Then it came out: the crop loan, whether the cotton would fail, whether he could be a better father than his own, how he would miss evenings with his friends. "I didn't want to burden you." Jaya took his hand. "I'm scared too. Tell me. Don't vanish." They decided to ask his brother for help at harvest, and Tejas promised to come to the next check-up at the health centre.

qa.q: Where did Tejas and Jaya talk that night?
qa.a: On the charpai.

qa.q: Why did Tejas keep his worries to himself?
qa.a: He felt pressured and afraid about money and fatherhood, and did not want to burden Jaya, so he tried to seem strong.

qa.q: What choice helped, and why?
qa.a: Tejas sharing his worries with Jaya; it let them plan together, with his brother's help at harvest and his promise to come to the check-up, instead of him withdrawing.

qa.q: How was Jaya affected by Tejas going quiet?
qa.a: She felt him slipping away and worried, which is why she asked where he had gone.

grounding: Illustrates an expectant father feeling pride and pressure about money, responsibility and freedom, keeping quiet to seem strong, then sharing with his partner.

passage:
Sunday, 1 am
Can't sleep. Latha is asleep with her hand on her belly, and I'm on the balcony pretending I'm fine.
Everyone says congratulations and you'll be a great dad. I nod. Inside it's: how do we manage on one salary for months, what if I turn out like my father, will I ever play Sunday cricket again. Then I feel guilty for even thinking about cricket.
I've been going quiet with Latha. Staying late at work. Last night she asked if I'm even happy about the baby. That scared me more than any of it.
Today I finally told Uday at the tea stall. He laughed, then got serious. "I felt exactly the same. Tell Latha. She'd rather know than guess."
Tomorrow at breakfast I'm telling her. All of it, even the cricket.
Jeevan

qa.q: Where did Jeevan finally tell Uday?
qa.a: At the tea stall.

qa.q: What is Jeevan feeling on the balcony?
qa.a: He feels proud yet anxious and pressured about money, turning out like his father and losing his freedom, and guilty for those thoughts.

qa.q: Why is telling Latha a good plan?
qa.a: Sharing the worries lets him support her instead of withdrawing, and she would rather know than guess.

qa.q: How might Latha be feeling about Jeevan's quietness?
qa.a: She seems hurt and unsure, even asking whether he is happy about the baby.

grounding: Shows an expectant father hiding worries about money, responsibility and freedom to seem strong, and choosing to share them instead of withdrawing.

passage:
Asif: bro u up
Uday: ya what's up
Asif: scan today. heartbeat. I cried in the car park
Uday: congrats!! big day
Asif: yeah. and now I can't breathe. rent, her leave, my job is shaky
Asif: plus I'm never going to see a football match again am I
Uday: haha. have u told Nazia any of this?
Asif: no. she's got enough on her plate. I'm supposed to be the strong one
Uday: being strong isn't the same as being silent. she probably thinks ur distant
Asif: she did ask why I've been so quiet
Uday: tell her. then we'll work out match nights. babies sleep sometimes 🙂
Asif: ok. telling her tonight

qa.q: What did Asif hear at the scan?
qa.a: The heartbeat.

qa.q: What was Asif feeling after the scan?
qa.a: He felt proud and moved, crying in the car park, but then anxious about rent, Nazia's leave and his job.

qa.q: What does Uday advise, and why is it wise?
qa.a: To tell Nazia, because being strong isn't the same as being silent, and sharing stops him seeming distant.

qa.q: How might Nazia see Asif's quietness?
qa.a: She may read it as distance and feel unsure, which is why she asked why he had been so quiet.

grounding: Shows an expectant father feeling pride and pressure about money and freedom but keeping quiet to seem strong, and a friend urging him to share.

passage: In the brass workshop at the edge of their village near Moradabad, Hrithik hammered harder than usual. Rehana was five months pregnant, the family was proud, and his mother had already sewn tiny kurtas. But at night he lay awake listening to the ceiling fan, adding numbers that never added up, thinking of the cricket team he would have to quit, wondering if he would shout like his own father. He came home later and later, ate in silence, and said "I'm fine" when Rehana asked. One evening she stood in the workshop doorway. "You're not fine. You're hiding from me." He put the hammer down. It all came out: the money, the freedom, the fear of becoming his father. Rehana sat on an upturned bucket. "I'm scared too. Let's be scared together, not separately." He walked home beside her for the first time in weeks.

qa.q: What had Hrithik's mother sewn?
qa.a: Tiny kurtas.

qa.q: What was Hrithik feeling at night?
qa.a: He felt anxious and pressured about money and freedom, and afraid of becoming like his father, even though the family was proud.

qa.q: What changed when Hrithik told Rehana everything?
qa.a: Sharing let them face the fears together instead of him withdrawing, so he walked home beside her.

qa.q: How had Rehana experienced his silence?
qa.a: She felt he was hiding from her, and she was scared too.

grounding: Shows an expectant father withdrawing under silent worries about money, freedom and becoming his father, and sharing them with his partner.

passage: Liam painted the spare room in their Dublin flat a pale yellow and told everyone he was buzzing about the baby. It was true. But at night he lay awake doing sums: rent, childcare, his contract ending in March. He already missed Saturday football with his mates, and felt guilty for missing it. He kept quiet, thinking Elif had enough to carry. Instead he went silent at dinner and worked late. One night Elif said, 'You've disappeared on me. What's going on?' He almost said 'nothing'. Then it all came out. Elif listened, then laughed softly. 'I'm scared about money too. Let's be scared together, and make a plan.'

qa.q: What colour did Liam paint the spare room?
qa.a: Pale yellow.

qa.q: What was Liam feeling at night?
qa.a: He felt anxious about money and his contract, and guilty for missing his freedom, while still excited about the baby.

qa.q: What changed when Liam shared his worries?
qa.a: Elif shared her own fears, and they could plan together instead of Liam withdrawing.

qa.q: How had Elif experienced Liam's silence?
qa.a: Elif felt he had disappeared on her, left alone and worried by the silence and late nights.

grounding: An expectant father hides worries about money and freedom until sharing them with his partner turns withdrawal into support.
